newsitem.title: ITALY: Scalfaro says Jewish settlements were "act of war".
newsitem.headline: Scalfaro says Jewish settlements were "act of war".

text.p: Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro on Thursday condemned the latest bombing attack in Jerusalem but said Israel's decision to build a Jewish settlement in the city's Arab sector had been an "act of war on peace".
"The bombs on the market in Jerusalem were a bomb on the hopes for peace," Scalfaro told reporters.
"But with a view which must be objective, I must say that the wound caused by the willingness to start the construction of homes in Jerusalem was also heavy," he said.
He added: "At that time no blood was shed but it was an act of war on peace..."
Israel suspended peace talks after a suicide attack at a Jewish market in Jerusalem on Wednesday killed 13 people and wounded 170.
Peace talks had been stalled since March when bulldozers began carving up a hill in Arab East Jerusalem where Israel plans 6,500 apartments for Jews.
Earlier this week Israel suspended a permit to build the enclave. Palestinians had made a renewal of peace talks conditional on an Israeli settlement freeze.
Scalfaro said that he would be visiting Israel soon and that his friendship with the Jewish state would allow him to speak frankly.
"I am going as a friend and it is friendship to say 'I think that you are wrong'," Scalfaro said.
